intro.narration: [excited] Heey, how do you estimate forty-nine times forty-eight in your head? Round, then multiply.

steps.narration: [curious] Here's our problem. Forty-nine times forty-eight.
[confident] Round each number to the nearest ten, then just multiply them.
steps.instruction: Round each factor to the nearest ten, then multiply

steps.narration: [confident] Forty-nine and forty-eight both round up to fifty. Fifty times fifty is two thousand five hundred.
steps.instruction: Round 49 and 48 up to 50, then multiply

steps.narration: [warm] Both rounded up, so that's a ceiling. The real answer, two thousand three hundred fifty-two, sits just below.
steps.instruction: Both rounded up, so 2500 is a ceiling

steps.narration: [thoughtful] But watch out. Round one up and one down, and you can't tell which side you land on. Forty-seven times forty-three rounds to two thousand, yet the truth is two thousand twenty-one.
